name: Cairns Art Gallery
funding: Cairns Regional Council gives 55 to 60 percent of operating costs. Cairns Art Gallery Foundation and Double R Arts Foundation fund works and artists. Cairns RSL Club funded 12 fellowships.
watch: Cairns RSL Club runs a gaming venue and funded fellowship rounds in 2021 and 2022. Double R founders are not named.
why_flagged: Cairns Regional Council gives 55 to 60 percent of operating costs. Cairns Art Gallery Foundation and Double R Arts Foundation fund works and artists. Cairns RSL Club funded 12 fellowships.
records_note: The gallery's own site posts nothing, but the ACNC register holds its reports and 2014 to 2025 accounts and names nine directors.

name: CaixaForum Madrid
funding: Fundación 'la Caixa' banking foundation endowment and exhibition tickets.
watch: SUT agreement in December 2025 restored guaranteed hours for Magmacultura contractor staff.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Fundación la Caixa posts accounts and governance reports 2014 to 2025 and names its trustees, with no donor list.

name: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
funding: Private foundation endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian's fortune; assets EUR 4.0bn at end 2025. It owned oil firm Partex until selling it to PTTEP in November 2019.
watch: Partex was about 18% of its investments. Ten protesters entered a Foundation conference in March 2016 and cited its ownership of Partex.
why_flagged: Private foundation endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian's fortune; assets EUR 4.0bn at end 2025. It owned oil firm Partex until selling it to PTTEP in November 2019.
records_note: Annual reports with certified accounts run from 2012 to 2025 and the board is listed; it publishes no donor list.

name: Camden Art Centre
funding: Arts Council England, DCMS, Bloomberg Philanthropies (programme support), trusts including AKO, Foyle, Freelands and Henry Moore, and patrons including Batia and Idan Ofer.
watch: Bloomberg title-sponsors New Contemporaries since 2001. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Camden was not named.
why_flagged: Bloomberg title-sponsors New Contemporaries since 2001. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Camden was not named.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the thank-you page names funders and patrons undated, and no trustees are listed.

name: Casa de la Arquitectura
funding: Ministry of Housing and Urban Agenda (MIVAU / MITMA) public appropriations.
watch: SUT union agreement resolved contractor Magmacultura hours dispute and retroactive pay.

name: Casa França-Brasil
funding: Rio de Janeiro state cultural centre; restoration backed by Fundação Roberto Marinho (media).
watch: Renamed Casa Brasil on 27 Jun 2025. Petrobras (under active campaign) is the current official sponsor, selected in its Novos Eixos call.
why_flagged: The former Casa França-Brasil now operates as Casa Brasil, with Petrobras as sponsor through its Novos Eixos call (Ícones da Cultura Brasileira line). The rename date is not confirmed.
records_note: Casa França-Brasil's site has no reports, accounts or board, only a sponsor logo bar that names Petrobras and state government bodies.

name: Centre Pompidou
funding: €130M annual operating budget. French Ministry of Culture subventions (over 65%), admissions, Friends of Centre Pompidou.
watch: €50M Saudi state pledge for the renovation.
why_flagged: €50M Saudi state pledge for the renovation.
records_note: Pompidou posts activity reports from 1973 to 2025 with a finance summary and a named 2025 patron list, but no accounts and no named board.

name: Centro Botín
funding: Run by Fundación Botín. Patrons: Fundación Mutua Madrileña, Fundación Prosegur, Roche España and two public tourism bodies. Strategic sponsors: Fundación EDP, Plenitude (Eni) and CESINE.
watch: Plenitude, controlled by Eni, sells gas and power in Spain from Santander. Fundación EDP is also a strategic sponsor. No protest found.
why_flagged: Run by Fundación Botín. Patrons: Fundación Mutua Madrileña, Fundación Prosegur, Roche España and two public tourism bodies. Strategic sponsors: Fundación EDP, Plenitude (Eni) and CESINE.
records_note: Fundación Botín posts annual reports from 2007 to 2025 and its trustees; the Centro Botín sponsor page names patrons and sponsors, undated.

name: Centro Cultural Tijuana
funding: Federal state company under Mexico's culture ministry. Modified budget MXN 132.9M for January to September 2025, of which MXN 88.0M accrued. A private patronato supports it.
watch: More than 250 Tijuana artists and writers boycotted the centre and its director Virgilio Muñoz for about three years, to 2011.
why_flagged: Federal state company under Mexico's culture ministry. Modified budget MXN 132.9M for January to September 2025, of which MXN 88.0M accrued. A private patronato supports it.
records_note: The centre posts federal budget and spending reports by quarter, but no annual report, funder list or board.

name: Centro de Arte La Estancia
funding: PDVSA, Venezuela's state oil company, runs the centre as its cultural arm. It still held shows in Caracas in June 2025. PDVSA remains under US blocking sanctions.
watch: General licence 52 (March 2026) permits some PDVSA dealings but leaves it listed. Its Maracaibo branch also runs shows.
why_flagged: PDVSA, Venezuela's state oil company, runs the centre as its cultural arm. It still held shows in Caracas in June 2025. PDVSA remains under US blocking sanctions.
records_note: Its parent PDVSA's website did not load and a search found only a 2010 PDVSA annual report, so its records are unchecked.

name: Centro León
location: Santiago de los Caballeros, Dominican Republic
watch: Tobacco founder money; museum includes a cigar-factory tour.
why_flagged: Tobacco founder money; museum includes a cigar-factory tour.
records_note: Centro León posts no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; its Amigos page describes membership fees but names no supporters.

name: Château de Versailles
funding: French state public establishment. Dior, The American Friends of Versailles and the Société des Amis de Versailles funded the Salon de Diane ceiling, reopened June 2026.
watch: Dior's parent LVMH drew €518M of tax relief for its Paris foundation, criticised by the Cour des comptes in 2018. Epstein links here are venue-only. See the Epstein cross-reference.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2003 to 2024 and names its board; shows no donor roster, since donors are engraved in the Château and credited per project.
